projectsSection.label: [PROJECTS] Case studies
projectsSection.title: What I've built.
projectsSection.lede: Six real projects — from an award-winning capstone to a system used by 230 people. Each with context, stack and technical decisions.

militrak.name: MiliTrak
militrak.tagline: Management system for a Brazilian Army training unit, in real production use
summary: MiliTrak is a management system for Tiro de Guerra units (Brazil's mandatory military training service), built to digitize the daily operation of a platoon. At its core is an RBAC access-control layer with four profiles (Sergeant, Instructor, Monitor, Rifleman), each with permissions configurable per tab, on top of daily roll call with individual logins. It also covers mission management with extra-duty hours, weekly duty rosters, a disciplinary module, physical fitness evaluation (TAF/TAT), equipment and uniform tracking, consolidated reporting, and automatic generation of official documents such as the CTSM and absence declarations.

The infrastructure runs entirely on free tiers — Supabase (database and auth) and Vercel (hosting) — an architectural constraint set from day one, since the system needs to keep running independent of ongoing maintenance. In production, it's actively used at unit TG-05-003 (Londrina), with expansion to other units as the next planned step.

stats.l: RBAC profiles with per-tab granular permissions

challenges: Granular permission matrix, configurable by role and by tab
Keeping everything scalable and secure on 100% free infrastructure
Generating official documents from dynamic data
Modeling a domain governed by specific military regulations
results: Formal commendation from the colonel at inspection, with a request to expand to other units
Direct feedback from sergeants and the colonel confirming a real operational speed-up

constria.name: Constria
summary: Constria is a multi-tenant SaaS for operational intelligence in civil construction, built as an alternative to systems that only log site data without turning it into decisions. The architecture is multi-tenant, with data isolation between organizations enforced via Row-Level Security (RLS) at the database level, and granular RBAC by module, role and site.

The technical MVP already covers identity, sessions, RBAC, multi-tenant structure, and subscription billing via Stripe with fully working webhooks. The next planned layer is an AI copilot using function calling over operational data, secured by the same RLS layer, to surface insights like which equipment spends the most time under maintenance, which project types run late most often, or which part categories arrive defective most — always paired with a suggested fix.

stats.l: Permissions by module, role and site

challenges: Row-Level Security (RLS) to isolate multiple organizations with real, not just on-paper, security
Modeling a robust data structure for a domain with a large volume and variety of information
Designing an AI copilot architecture with cost control and data-access security
results: Technical MVP finished (identity, sessions, RBAC, organization and Stripe subscriptions), still no set launch date

trabalho-amigo.name: Trabalho Amigo
trabalho-amigo.tagline: Services marketplace — top-grade capstone project, later rewritten solo
trabalho-amigo.role: Backend + database on the team (v1) · solo rewrite (v2)
summary: Trabalho Amigo is a services marketplace connecting clients to independent professionals, with a review system to reduce the risk of bad hires. V1 was built in plain PHP with MySQL, with a complete backend, database design, and part of the frontend.

V2 is a full rewrite of the same business domain with a decoupled architecture: a Laravel backend and a separate Next.js/TypeScript frontend consuming it as an API. It's roughly 70% complete and currently paused, keeping the same client↔professional matching and provider-review model from v1.

stats.l: V1 in plain PHP/MySQL, v2 rewritten in Laravel
Decoupled backend and frontend in v2

challenges: Team collaboration with a clear division of roles and a focus on performance (v1)
Rewriting a full, already-validated system solo, from scratch, with a more professional stack (v2)
Modeling a marketplace with provider reviews and client↔professional matching
results: Top grade from the capstone evaluation board, with explicit praise

dubflow.name: DubFlow
summary: DubFlow is a platform for dubbing communities to organize content by title, season and episode, publish audio and video, credit characters and voice actors, and run an editorial approval flow before publishing. Real-time communication — notifications, status updates, social interactions — runs over WebSockets, with its own JWT-based auth instead of a third-party provider.

The product ran in production for 2 to 4 months, with real usage from a few dozen accounts. It's currently paused, but the real-time architecture and the credit/collaboration model remain the base for a possible relaunch.

stats.l: Media publishing with an editorial approval step

challenges: A large feature scope to sustain as a solo developer
Real-time architecture (WebSockets) for live notifications and interactions
An editorial collaboration flow with approval before publishing
results: Product validated in practice, with dozens of real users coming to use the platform

cybersec-lab.name: CyberSec Lab
cybersec-lab.tagline: Incident-investigation simulator built around a Kali Linux desktop
summary: CyberSec Lab simulates a full Kali Linux desktop entirely in plain JavaScript, with no framework: top panel, app launcher, file manager, notes, and a terminal with over 30 SSH CLI commands implemented from scratch, with no real shell behind it.

The scenario: the simulated server shows a sequence of signs of compromise, and the player has to investigate the environment, gather IOCs (indicators of compromise) using the terminal's own commands, fix the problem, and name the type of attack. Difficulty ramps up progressively each round, with new attack scenarios.

stats.l: SSH terminal commands built from scratch
Investigation driven by indicators of compromise

challenges: Implementing a believable, functional SSH CLI in plain JavaScript alone
Recreating a full desktop interface with no framework
Designing a coherent investigation scenario, with enough clues to reach the diagnosis
results: Already tested by other people, with positive feedback on how real the simulated environment feels

pett-love.name: Pett-Love
pett-love.tagline: Hiring-challenge answer key, and a personal frontend benchmark
pett-love.role: Author of the answer key (Clickweb) + personal rebuild
summary: Pett-Love is a rebuild of a front-end hiring challenge (originally Clickweb's answer key for evaluating candidates), implemented in React + TypeScript with Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Motion for animation.

The implementation goes beyond the original Figma scope: besides the base screens, it includes a blog, contact page, login, and integration with a public animal API. The engineering focus was code quality and UX within a fixed layout's constraints, with specific attention to accessibility and performant animation, using Biome for lint and formatting.

stats.l: Beyond the Figma scope (blog, contact, login, animal API)

challenges: Shipping beyond the requested scope without losing quality, on a short timeline
Accessibility within a layout with limited freedom
Animation that adds to the UX without hurting performance
